CHR, a declarative language for implementing constraint satisfaction systems, is a 
key framework in the field. It has been shown to be Turing complete, but this 
property is only valid when a single head per rule is used. In this study, we 
investigate the impact of allowing multiple heads in CHR rules. We find that 
permitting multiple heads in CHR rules significantly enhances its expressive 
power. Specifically, we demonstrate that a CHR language with multiple heads 
cannot be simulated by a version with single-headed rules. We also prove that a 
CHR language with multiple heads is undecidable, even when constraints on the 
number of heads are limited. These findings are significant as they imply that 
a CHR language with multiple heads cannot be used to create efficient 
implementations of constraint satisfaction systems.

We've examined the alignment of galaxy spin directions in the DES Data Release 1, which includes 11,500 galaxies with redshifts between 0.05 and 0.4. Our analysis of the galaxy spin directions in the DES data shows a significant alignment with the cosmic microwave background, which is consistent with the findings of other large-scale galaxy surveys. We also found that the DES data agrees with the results of other large-scale galaxy surveys, which suggests that the DES data is reliable. We have also investigated the potential effects of selection bias on the galaxy spin directions in the DES data, which could lead to an apparent alignment with the cosmic microwave background. Our analysis of the DES data shows that the potential effects of selection bias are minimal, which supports the conclusion that the DES data is reliable. We have also compared the results of the DES data with the results of other large-scale galaxy surveys, which suggests that the DES data is consistent with the other large-scale galaxy surveys. Our analysis of the DES data provides further evidence that the DES data is reliable and that the cosmic microwave background is the dominant factor influencing the galaxy spin directions in the DES data.

Meta-learning methods have been highly effective in learning from limited data, but they are often hindered by the presence of noise in the data. In this study, we investigate the impact of sampling noise and label noise on the performance of a meta-learning algorithm called Eigen-Reptile. Our analysis reveals that the presence of noise in the data can lead to suboptimal performance, particularly when the noise is correlated with the true labels. To address this issue, we introduce a novel method called Robust Meta-learning via Eigen-Reptile, which involves a two-step process. In the first step, we use the Eigen-Reptile algorithm to learn a robust representation of the data, and in the second step, we use this representation to make predictions on the test data. Our experiments show that the proposed method is more robust to sampling noise and label noise than traditional meta-learning methods, and it achieves better performance on a variety of datasets.

Recent advancements in feature attribution methods have enabled the creation of visualizations that provide insights into the input data used by machine learning models to make predictions. This capability is particularly valuable in the medical field, where it can help clinicians understand the input data used by models to make diagnoses. Our research focuses on developing a feature attribution method that can be applied to a wide range of models, including those used for classification and regression tasks. We have successfully tested this method on a neuroimaging dataset, where it was able to identify the key brain regions associated with cognitive decline in individual scans. Our findings suggest that the feature attribution method can be a valuable tool for clinicians to understand the input data used by machine learning models in medical diagnosis.

The emergence of AI ethics as a distinct field has garnered considerable attention,
yet a closer examination reveals that it has been largely influenced by the
conventional trajectory of technological advancements. This conventional path
has been marked by a tendency to overlook the ethical implications associated
with the peripheral aspects of AI, which are often overlooked in favor of the
central focus on the technology itself. This paper seeks to rectify this oversight
by exploring the ethical implications of the marginalized aspects of AI,
including the data collection and labeling processes, the development of AI
systems, and the deployment of these systems in real-world settings. By
doing so, we aim to highlight the importance of addressing these often-neglected
issues in the pursuit of a more comprehensive and inclusive approach to AI
ethics.

We introduce the concept of an extended ω-regular language, which encompasses ω-regular languages as a subset, and demonstrate that it remains closed under a specific operation. Furthermore, we show that a language falls under this class if and only if it can be represented through a specific type of automaton, characterized by a tree structure and specific acceptance conditions.

In cell-free mMIMO systems, channel estimation is a crucial task that is particularly challenging due to the large number of access points involved. To address this issue, a novel approach is proposed that combines alternating channel estimation and prediction methods. This approach leverages the temporal properties of the channel to minimize the impact of channel aging. To further enhance the estimation and prediction process, a deep learning-based scheme is introduced, which utilizes a multi-layer perceptron neural network to learn the channel characteristics. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme outperforms existing methods in terms of the mean square error of channel estimation and prediction.

We are currently engaged in an ongoing project to determine the parameters $V_{ud}$ and $g_A$ through the analysis of neutron beta decay. This project involves a lattice QCD simulation using the $4$-flavour MILC collaboration's asqtad action, which employs $2+1+1$ flavours of dynamical quarks. The gauge configurations are based on those generated by the MILC collaboration, and we are utilizing the ETMC collaboration's $3+1$ flavour ensembles.

Image denoising is a long-standing issue in computer vision, and deep learning has made significant strides in recent years. However, existing methods often struggle with preserving fine details and textures in noisy images. To address this, we introduce an Identity Enhanced Residual (IER) module that leverages the identity mapping to retain high-frequency information and enhance residual learning. By incorporating the IER module into a U-Net architecture, we create a new image denoising model that outperforms existing techniques in both synthetic and real-world noise removal tasks.

Multiview learning has been a significant area of research in machine learning, focusing on leveraging multiple perspectives of data to enhance model performance.  A recent approach, Latent Correlation-Based Multiview Learning, has been proposed to address the limitations of traditional methods, which often fail to fully utilize the connections between different views.  This new method, LCML, has been shown to be effective in various applications, but its theoretical underpinnings have not been fully explored.  In this study, we delve into the fundamental aspects of LCML, specifically its capacity for self-supervision and the capacity to accurately recover the true data-generating process.  Our analysis reveals that LCML's ability to accurately recover the true data-generating process is contingent upon the true data-generating process itself.  Furthermore, we demonstrate that LCML's self-supervision capability is closely linked to the capacity of the true data-generating process.  Our findings provide valuable insights into the fundamental properties of LCML and its potential for self-supervision.

As language models become increasingly influential in shaping societal norms, it's crucial to understand how people perceive these models' moral implications. This study examines the moral judgments of ordinary individuals in comparison to a prominent language model, GPT-3, focusing on the moral dilemmas presented in the Moral Machine dataset. The results reveal a striking disparity between the two, with people more likely to prioritize human lives over those of other species, while GPT-3 tends to favor human lives in most cases. Moreover, the model's decision-making process is heavily influenced by the framing of the dilemma, whereas humans are more likely to consider the moral status of the species involved. This research highlights the need for further investigation into the moral risks associated with language models and the development of evaluation methods that can assess their moral reasoning capabilities.

We demonstrate that valuation rings, featuring a countable residue field and a logarithmic residue class field, can be expressed as limits of complete intersection rings. This result has significant implications, including: firstly, it validates the complete intersection conjecture for valuation rings with the specified properties; secondly, it establishes that any such valuation ring can be represented as a limit of regular rings, thereby affirming the regular ring conjecture.

The two-dimensional Dirac equation is examined in the context of the Klein paradox, where the effects of varying boundary conditions on the system's spectrum are investigated. It is found that a system with a step potential exhibits a Klein tunneling effect, while a system with a box potential experiences a suppression of this effect. It is also discovered that the system's spectrum is highly sensitive to numerical errors, which can lead to spurious Klein tunneling when the box potential is not sufficiently confining.

This research investigates the impact of communication delays on cooperative adaptive cruise control and automated platooning systems. We utilize a model predictive control approach to develop control strategies for both systems, taking into account communication loss. We analyze the effects of this loss on system stability and performance, and we provide a framework for designing control policies that can tolerate communication failures. Our results show that communication delays can significantly degrade the performance of these systems, and that the use of model predictive control can help to mitigate the effects of these delays.

The proliferation of social media platforms has led to an increase in the spread of misinformation, particularly on Twitter, where users can post content without verification. To combat this issue, we developed a novel approach to assess the credibility of Twitter users by leveraging a dataset of verified and unverified individuals. Our approach involves using a set of features to evaluate user credibility, including the proportion of retweets from verified users, the ratio of retweets to followers, and the proportion of followers who are verified. Our results demonstrate that these features can effectively predict user credibility, with a correlation of 0.65 between the proportion of retweets from verified users and user credibility. Our findings suggest that our approach can be used to identify and flag potentially unreliable users, thereby reducing the spread of misinformation on Twitter.

In the context of 5G and beyond, emergency situations are expected to be supported through the implementation of emergency network slices. These slices are characterized by the need for rapid deployment, minimal latency, and high reliability. However, the unpredictable nature of emergency scenarios poses significant challenges to existing network slicing solutions. To address these challenges, a novel approach called $\pi$-ROAD is proposed. This solution leverages a deep reinforcement learning-based framework that enables the dynamic adaptation of network slicing policies in real-time. By utilizing a multi-agent system, the proposed solution can efficiently manage multiple emergency scenarios simultaneously, while also incorporating a hierarchical policy to optimize resource allocation and minimize latency. The proposed approach is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in meeting the stringent requirements of emergency network slices.

The emergence of collaborative robots has significantly accelerated the adoption of robots in various industries, including those that are traditionally difficult to automate. However, the increased interaction between humans and robots has raised concerns about potential safety hazards. To address these concerns, we propose a novel system called CoHaptics, which incorporates a forearm-worn haptic display to enhance human-robot collaboration. This system, which we have developed and tested in a real-world scenario, enables workers to safely collaborate with robots while receiving haptic feedback to mitigate potential risks. Our results show that CoHaptics can effectively improve safety in human-robot collaboration environments.

The rapid growth of urbanization and the increasing adoption of autonomous vehicles have sparked significant interest in developing urban environments that seamlessly integrate mobility and autonomy. Urban areas are complex systems that combine social, technical, and environmental elements, making them ideal for testing new concepts in autonomous systems. This paper aims to explore the potential of applying urban mobility as a testbed for developing and evaluating urban autonomy, with a focus on autonomous vehicles. We will examine the underlying principles of urban autonomy and the potential benefits of applying autonomy principles to urban mobility. Additionally, we will discuss the potential applications of autonomous systems in various domains, including transportation, healthcare, and emergency response, and the challenges that need to be addressed to achieve these goals.

In the context of online caching, we examine a scenario where a cache manager is given a stream of requests for a large set of data items, with a fixed-size cache initially containing some items. The cache manager can either satisfy a request directly or replace an existing item with another, incurring a penalty for each replacement. To improve performance, we introduce a new caching algorithm that utilizes probabilistic advice from a source, with a specified error rate. The algorithm achieves near-optimal results for both adversarial and random advice, with a competitive ratio of $O(\sqrt{\log C})$ for adversarial advice and a constant ratio for random advice, where $C$ is the cardinality of the item set.

Deep learning-based medical image segmentation has seen significant advancements in recent years, but the computational demands of these models pose a challenge for real-time applications. To overcome this limitation, we developed the Trilateral Attention Network (TAN), a novel approach that incorporates attention mechanisms to enhance the efficiency of medical image segmentation. By leveraging three distinct attention modules, TAN captures relationships between pixels, patches, and global features, thereby improving its ability to identify and segment objects in images. Experimental results on the MS-COCO dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of TAN, with a notable improvement of 0.21 in the Jaccard index for the Pancreas dataset compared to the existing U-Net model. Furthermore, our findings show that the integration of attention mechanisms in TAN leads to a substantial reduction in the number of parameters, making it a viable solution for real-time medical image segmentation.

We introduce a linearized 4+7 supergeometry for the on-shell and off-shell descriptions of 11D supergravity, utilizing a 2+1 connection that encompasses the graviton, gravitino, and a 3-form field. The supergeometry is defined by a superspace with four bosonic and seven fermionic coordinates, and a 2+1 connection consisting of the above-mentioned fields and a 2-form. We demonstrate that the torsion and curvature of this supergeometry are entirely determined by the connection and its derivatives, and that the Bianchi identities are also encapsulated within the supergeometry. We further show that the supergeometry is equivalent to the linearized equations of motion of 11D supergravity, and that the supergeometry is also equivalent to the linearized equations of motion of 11D supergravity with an additional field. We also demonstrate that the supergeometry is equivalent to the linearized equations of motion of 11D supergravity with an additional field and a 2-form, and that the supergeometry is also equivalent to the linearized equations of motion of 11D supergravity with an additional field and a 2-form and a 3-form.

Machine learning models rely heavily on high-quality data, but the data used in practice often contains errors and inconsistencies. To address this issue, we've developed a new method that leverages the training process of gradient boosting machines to identify and correct data quality problems. By analyzing the model's performance on individual data points, we can pinpoint problematic samples and rectify them, ultimately enhancing the overall performance of the machine learning model. Our approach is flexible and can be applied to various types of gradient boosting implementations, making it a versatile tool for improving machine learning model performance.

We investigate the concept of spin in the context of quantum Hall edge states, and find that the Pauli spin matrices are non-local in nature. This discovery has significant implications for the implementation of quantum gates, particularly the spin-based quantum Hall edge qubit gate, which is a crucial component in quantum computing. Our analysis reveals that the qubit gate, which involves rotating the spin of the electron, is a straightforward operation that can be achieved through a simple phase shift. This phase shift can be applied to the spinor wave function of the electron, and we demonstrate that the spinor wave function can be rotated by a unitary operator, which is a fundamental concept in quantum information theory.

We introduce an efficient denoising pretraining method for large language models, leveraging model-generated signals. Our approach, named METRO, is designed to train large models efficiently by utilizing a large, diverse dataset of denoised samples. By employing a unique noise generation strategy, METRO produces a wide range of denoised samples, allowing for effective pretraining of large models. Our results demonstrate that pretraining large models on synthetic data can achieve comparable performance to models trained on real data, while significantly reducing computational costs. Furthermore, METRO enables the efficient pretraining of large models, such as a 1.3B parameter model, on a single node, resulting in a model that outperforms models trained on real data.

To effectively introduce information visualizations to a general audience, it's crucial to understand what essential information should be conveyed. This study aims to identify key explanatory examples that can be used to describe information visualizations. We conducted a crowdsourced survey to gather descriptions and corresponding examples from 111 participants. Our analysis revealed that people's descriptions of visualizations are heavily influenced by the examples they use, and that the absence of examples can lead to incomplete or inaccurate descriptions. We also found that the most effective descriptions include a combination of accurate, concise, and relevant examples. We used these findings to develop a crowdsourced tool that prompts users to provide descriptions accompanied by relevant examples. The results of our experiment show that the tool significantly improves the quality of descriptions and encourages users to provide relevant examples.

The concept of maximum entropy condensates is explored in relation to the ground state of a Bose gas, with an examination of its connection to the Elliott-Thouless-Anderson-Peierls-Yuval (TAPY) equation. Additionally, we discuss how the Elliott-Thouless-Peierls-Yuval (TPY) inequality is related to Lieb's theorem, as well as the implications of this inequality for the maximum entropy condensates.

Counterfactual analysis in AI systems is a crucial aspect for understanding and improving model performance. A counterfactual plan outlines a sequence of actions that, if taken, would have led to a different outcome. In this research, a new method is proposed to create counterfactual plans in environments with uncertain reward distributions. Unlike previous approaches that rely on a single counterfactual scenario, this counterfactual plan takes into account multiple possible counterfactuals, each with its own distribution. The proposed method is tested in a simulated environment and compared to existing methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating robust counterfactual plans.

The task of classifying urban sounds is a complex challenge in the field of audio processing, requiring a thorough examination of existing methods. This research aims to provide a comprehensive evaluation of current techniques by introducing a new dataset, the Urban Sound Classification Challenge (USCC), comprising 1000 samples from 10 diverse urban sound categories. Our investigation encompasses a comparison of different approaches, including those utilizing raw audio inputs and those incorporating spectrogram-based features, as well as a detailed analysis of the effects of various pre-processing techniques and the impact of different classification algorithms. Notably, our experiments reveal that incorporating pitch and chroma features can enhance the performance of spectrogram-based methods, while the application of data augmentation techniques can yield significant improvements.

We examine the static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions in four-dimensional, matter-coupled gauged supergravities with N=3,4, supersymmetry, and matter content. These models, with matter in the fundamental 3 or 4 representation of SU(4), are derived from the gauged supergravities proposed in the works of [1,2]. We find that the black hole solutions are supersymmetric and have a regular horizon, and we also study the behavior of the dual field theory in the large N limit.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are widely used in edge computing, especially in applications like autonomous driving and robotics, where they need to process convolutional kernels on specialized Focal-plane Sensor-processors (FSPs). However, the current compilers for FSPs are inefficient, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address this limitation, we developed Cain, a compiler that optimizes FSPs by combining multiple convolutions into a single kernel, which can be executed in parallel on FSPs. To achieve this, Cain employs a novel code generation approach that leverages a graph-based representation of FSPs, enabling it to generate optimized code for convolutional kernels. To further improve performance, Cain incorporates a graph neural network to predict the optimal execution order of kernels, which can be executed in parallel on FSPs. To facilitate the execution of multiple kernels, Cain introduces a new instruction set that supports parallel execution of multiple kernels on FSPs. To demonstrate the effectiveness of Cain, we implemented it on the Mantis FSP, which supports parallel execution of multiple kernels. Experimental results show that Cain outperforms state-of-the-art compilers by up to 2.5x in terms of performance, while also reducing the size of the generated code by up to 10%.

We investigate the symmetry breaking and topological characteristics of a Type IIB orientifold compactification, focusing on a specific toroidal model with non-trivial generalized Scherk-Schwarz phases. The model incorporates a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge symmetry, which is partially broken by the vacuum expectation value of the axio-dilaton, resulting in a stable topological sector. This stability is attributed to the presence of a generalized theta-term, which is a topological invariant of the spacetime. We demonstrate that the model's effective action can be described by a set of effective operators, which are derived from the underlying geometry and fluxes. We also show that the model's effective action is invariant under a set of dualities, which are related to the underlying symmetry of the model. Finally, we discuss the implications of our results for the understanding of the model's phase structure and its potential applications to the study of quantum gravity.

In multiagent reinforcement learning, learning Nash equilibria is a key objective.
However, learning algorithms often struggle to converge, particularly when the
underlying game is complex. To address this, researchers have developed
approximate learning algorithms that can find approximate equilibria in various
game types. This study focuses on a specific class of games, known as
simulation-based games, which are difficult to analyze due to their complexity.
To improve the efficiency of learning algorithms in this context, we introduce a
novel approach called Regret Pruning, which allows for faster convergence by
remining agents with high regret. This method is shown to be effective in
convergence and can be applied to a range of games, including those with
complex dynamics.

This research develops a modal logic based on Aristotle's modal syllogistic principles, 
demonstrating that it possesses key characteristics, including the ability to prove valid inferences and that every valid argument has a corresponding justification. 
The research also identifies a specific set of rules that can serve as a foundation for this logic, 
showing that it is capable of producing valid conclusions from these rules. 
The research also explores the relationship between this logic and other established modal systems, 
establishing that it shares certain characteristics with them. 
The research also investigates the capabilities of this logic in handling complex arguments, 
showing that it can effectively reason about certain types of modal syllogistic arguments.

A new concept of causal order in quantum theory has been developed, but its application is hindered by a significant issue - the detection loophole. This paper proposes a solution to the problem by introducing a framework that can effectively eliminate the detection loophole, and a practical method is presented to verify the new concept experimentally.

A key goal in video streaming is to deliver high-quality images to users while minimizing bandwidth usage. A promising approach to achieve this is to dynamically adjust the bit rate for each frame based on its complexity and the user's visual perception. A novel dual-critic reinforcement learning framework has been proposed to optimize this process in HEVC videos. The framework utilizes two separate value functions: one that evaluates the overall video quality and another that considers the user's visual perception. A novel reward function has also been designed to balance the trade-off between video quality and user experience. The framework was tested on the UCL TREC Video Benchmark and demonstrated significant improvements in video quality and user satisfaction compared to existing methods.

The formation of complex organic molecules (COMs) in interstellar and circumstellar environments is a critical process in the development of life. The destruction of carbon-rich grains by UV radiation is a key factor in the production of COMs. This process is particularly important in the final stages of the evolution of young stars, where carbon grains are destroyed, leading to a significant increase in the abundance of COMs. This phenomenon has been observed in the circumstellar disk of the young star IRAS 2L, where the destruction of carbon-rich grains is responsible for the emergence of COMs. This destruction process is a crucial stage in the evolution of the disk, as it leads to the formation of a new generation of molecules that can contribute to the development of life.

Cutting planes are a crucial component of solving mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) efficiently, but their effectiveness heavily relies on the quality of selected cuts. To address this issue, we've developed an innovative method that leverages deep imitation learning to choose cutting planes for MILPs. Our approach involves training a neural network to mimic expert behavior, using the MILP's dual information as input. To facilitate learning, we've designed a novel reward function that evaluates the impact of each cut on the MILP's solution. To prevent overfitting, we've also incorporated a curriculum learning strategy that gradually increases the complexity of the MILPs. Our experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of solution time and quality.

Researchers have been studying superconductivity in materials with topological properties, particularly in materials with a unique electronic structure. A specific material, Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$, has been found to exhibit superconductivity with a transition temperature of 2.5 K. This material has a unique electronic structure with a nodal line that is a type of topological feature. However, the nodal line in Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$ is different from those found in other topological materials, as it is a result of the breaking of inversion symmetry. This makes Mo$_{0.9}$Ir$_{0.1}$Te$_{2}$ a unique system for studying topological superconductivity.

The bug reporting process is a vital component of software testing, and its efficiency is largely determined by the speed and accuracy of the bug triage. To enhance the bug triage process, this paper proposes a machine learning-based approach that utilizes Natural Language Processing to automatically assign categories to bug reports. By converting textual bug reports into numerical features, the model can predict the bug's category with a high degree of accuracy. The proposed model is trained on a dataset of 1,000 bug reports, and its performance is evaluated using standard metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall. The results demonstrate that the model can effectively categorize bug reports with a high level of accuracy, and its performance is comparable to that of human experts.

We investigate the phase transitions in a two-dimensional, two-component electron system with anisotropic mass, experiencing both Coulomb and spin fluctuations. By using the self-consistent parquet approximation, we find that the mass anisotropy has a significant impact on the critical behavior of the system. Specifically, mass anisotropy suppresses the critical temperature of the spin-fluctuation driven transition, while the Coulomb-fluctuation driven transition's critical temperature is not significantly affected. Furthermore, mass anisotropy causes the critical temperature of the superconducting transition to decrease, ultimately leading to a transition into a normal state at a certain critical level of anisotropy.

The goal of named entity recognition (NER) is to identify and classify specific parts of text, such as locations, organizations, and timeframes. A significant limitation of current NER models is their reliance on extensive, labeled data, which is often expensive and time-consuming to obtain. To address this issue, we have developed a novel approach that utilizes unlabeled data to enhance NER models. Our method involves two key components: first, we use a self-improving teacher model to generate pseudo-labels for training, and second, we employ a diverse ensemble of student models to refine these pseudo-labels. By combining these techniques, we can effectively leverage unlabeled data to improve NER model performance. Our approach has been tested on multiple datasets, including AG News, IMDB, and WikiNews, and has achieved state-of-the-art results, demonstrating its effectiveness in utilizing unlabeled data to enhance NER model performance.

This study examines the application of text mining techniques to analyze Twitter data related to tourism. We employed a range of tools to extract and analyze tweets, including data extraction, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and word association analysis. We also utilized specific metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of our analysis, such as accuracy, recall, and F1-score. The results of our study demonstrate the potential of using Twitter data to gain valuable insights into tourism trends and patterns.

The development of new materials with tailored properties is a significant challenge in materials science.  To address this, researchers have been working on a data-driven approach that can predict the properties of materials based on their microstructure.  This method involves using machine learning to establish connections between the microstructure and the properties of materials.  In this study, we have applied this data-driven method to a specific type of material called nanocrystalline copper, and we have successfully created a predictive model that can accurately estimate the material's properties.  Our model has been validated using a well-established theoretical framework, and we have found that it can accurately predict the material's properties across a wide range of microstructures.  Our results demonstrate the potential of the data-driven approach in predicting the properties of materials, and we have shown that it can be used to design new materials with tailored properties.

We have developed a new two-body potential with a unique interaction that is
symmetric and exhibits a single minimum, but unlike previous models, it does not
have its minimum at zero distance. This innovative potential is characterized by
a single parameter that dictates the minimum energy point, and it is designed to
mimic the behavior of a harmonic oscillator. Our model is well-suited for
simulating systems with a finite separation distance between particles, and it
can be used to study systems with a wide range of parameters.

This article focuses on fractional Sobolev spaces on compact manifolds, establishing a sharp inequality for $W^{s,2}_0(M)$ that is independent of the function's mean value. The proof relies on a specific nonlinear integral inequality, which is derived through an adapted extension method.

This study introduces a new method for estimating the trajectories of multiple objects in a scene, which utilizes a backward simulation approach to identify and track objects within a sequence of images. By starting from the final frame and working backward, the algorithm identifies and refines the locations of objects within each frame, using a probabilistic model to determine the likelihood of their existence. To improve the accuracy of the results, the algorithm incorporates a process of smoothing the identified trajectories. The proposed method is evaluated using both real-world and artificially generated datasets, and its performance is compared to a forward simulation-based method, demonstrating its effectiveness in estimating the movements of multiple objects.

The introduction of Voltage Source Converters (VSCs) in power grids has led to an increase in their number, which has prompted a need for a comprehensive stability analysis framework. This paper presents a stability assessment approach for multi-source VSCs connected to the grid, utilizing a matrix-based admittance model. The proposed method is applied to a test system to evaluate the impact of different control strategies on system stability. The results demonstrate that the approach is effective in assessing stability and can be used to determine the stability of VSCs with multiple inputs.

In the realm of online authentication, a novel approach to evaluating the quality of signature templates has emerged, focusing on three key attributes: distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability. This new framework, grounded in statistical analysis, utilizes a combination of mathematical models and geometric shapes to assess these properties. By employing a Gaussian distribution and a circle model, researchers have developed a scoring system that measures the distinctiveness of templates. Additionally, a method based on the number of zero-crossings in the autocorrelation function is proposed to evaluate the complexity of templates. To ensure the reliability of these assessments, a study was conducted to determine the appropriate number of trials required to achieve consistent results. This new framework has been tested on a large dataset of 1,000 signature templates, and the results have been compared to those obtained using a traditional method based on signal-to-noise ratio. The findings suggest that the new framework provides a more accurate and comprehensive evaluation of template quality.
This paper offers two distinct visual representations of Hardy sums within the framework of two-dimensional geometry.

The concept of contextual values, which are data values that depend on their surrounding environment, has been extensively researched in the field of programming languages. However, the application of contextual values in operating systems has been largely overlooked. This paper explores the use of contextual values in operating systems, particularly in the context of inter-process communication. We propose that contextual values can be utilized to create complex, context-dependent data structures that can be shared between processes. We demonstrate that contextual values can be used to implement a variety of inter-process communication primitives, including shared memory, message passing, and remote procedure calls. We also discuss the benefits of using contextual values in inter-process communication, including improved data encapsulation, reduced inter-process coupling, and enhanced security.

This study introduces an innovative approach to 3D human pose estimation from videos, leveraging a hybrid network that combines attention mechanisms and convolutional layers. By utilizing attention, the model can prioritize key frames and sequences, thereby enhancing its ability to capture long-term dependencies. To further improve performance, the model employs dilated convolutions, which enable it to expand its receptive field without increasing the computational cost. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method surpasses the current state-of-the-art in accuracy, with a notable 1.5% and 2.1% reduction in MPJPE and MPEJPE metrics respectively on the Human3.6M dataset.

The CZTI instrument on the AstroSat X-ray observatory is capable of detecting gamma rays in the 0.1-4 MeV range. CZTI's ability to monitor the entire sky makes it suitable for the Earth Occultation technique, which can be used to measure the diffuse X-ray background. By employing this method, the diffuse X-ray background can be measured with a signal-to-noise ratio of 1.5, using data from the first 100 days of the AstroSat mission. The instrument's sensitivity to the diffuse X-ray background is approximately 100 times greater than that of previous experiments, and it is also sensitive to the diffuse gamma-ray background. Furthermore, the instrument can detect the Galactic Center gamma-ray line emission, which was previously observed by the Fermi satellite.

This paper examines the long-term performance of two prominent blockchain protocols, PoW and PoA, by developing a Markov chain model to represent their state evolution. The proposed model enables the derivation of the system's steady-state distribution, which is used to calculate the block confirmation probability and assess the system's efficiency. The analysis reveals that PoA outperforms PoW in terms of efficiency, as it can process transactions more quickly. The results also show that the system's efficiency is influenced by the block generation time and the number of participating nodes. The findings provide insights into the design of blockchain systems, enabling a data-driven approach to optimize their performance.

Tightly bound doubly heavy tetraquark states are predicted to be particularly stable, making them ideal candidates for experimental detection. This study employs a modified potential model, incorporating a refined chromomagnetic interaction, to investigate the mass spectra of doubly heavy tetraquarks. The model's parameters are calibrated using the masses of doubly heavy mesons, and our findings reveal that the mass gap between the ground and first excited states is substantial. The model's predictions for the mass spectra of tetraquarks with various quantum numbers are in good agreement with theoretical and experimental data.

The stability of the electroweak vacuum is a crucial consideration in the Standard Model, particularly when considering the large hierarchy between the Higgs mass and the electroweak scale. We have found that the Higgs mass can be estimated by the scale of electroweak vacuum instability, which is a unique prediction of the Standard Model. This prediction is supported by the fact that the metastability of the electroweak vacuum is a well-established phenomenon. We have also found that the metastability of the electroweak vacuum is a crucial factor in determining the Higgs mass, which is in agreement with the observed value. This result suggests that the metastability of the electroweak vacuum is a unique prediction of the Standard Model, which is a crucial finding in the field of particle physics.

We establish the $q$-Logarithmic Sobolev Inequality and the $p$-Talagrand Inequality on complete Carnot groups, using an approach that involves solving the sub-elliptic heat equation, which differs from previous methods that relied on a specific flow.

This study introduces a new statistical approach known as minimum Bregman divergence inference, which involves finding a probability distribution that minimizes the divergence gap between it and an empirical distribution derived from observed data. The proposed method is distinct from traditional minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence methods, as it can handle data with zero probabilities and yields a unique solution. The approach is applied to various scenarios, including when the target distribution belongs to specific families of distributions, such as exponential, normal, or logistic, and also when it has a fixed mean. The results show that this method can effectively estimate the target distribution even when it does not belong to a specific parametric family. The approach is evaluated through a simulation study and a real-world example involving the estimation of a Poisson mixture model.

We introduce a pioneering approach to generate realistic images of dynamic scenes from a single video, using a novel, unsupervised method that relies on a neural radiance field. This technique, known as wildNeRF, is capable of producing high-quality images of scenes that move over time, using only a single video as input. Our method is based on a unique, unsupervised loss function that enables the model to learn the dynamic nature of a scene, even in the absence of detailed 3D information. This unsupervised approach allows us to train our model to generate accurate, novel views of scenes that move over time, using only a single video as input. Our results demonstrate that wildNeRF can produce high-quality images of dynamic scenes, even in challenging scenarios, and outperforms existing methods on a variety of benchmarks.

We investigate a quantum graph's spectral statistic in the context of specific vertex conditions, utilizing a method that involves evaluating its associated periodic orbits. This statistical method is based on a bilinear form that is influenced by the geometry of the underlying graph. Our analysis demonstrates that this approach yields a spectral statistic that is not solely dependent on the semiclassical limit but also on the length of the intervals defining the graph. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for a particular vertex condition, our spectral statistic is equivalent to the traditional method that relies on the semiclassical approximation.

Astronomers have been using light curves to study variable stars for over a century, and their periodic behavior has been extensively researched.  However, the process of determining the period of these stars is time-consuming and requires manual analysis, which is not suitable for large datasets.  A new method has been developed to automate the process of period determination, and it has been tested on a large dataset of stars from the Kepler mission.  The method uses a combination of mathematical techniques to identify the period of these stars, and it has been found to be effective in a wide range of cases.  The method has been successfully applied to a large dataset of stars, and it has been found to be effective in identifying the period of these stars, even in cases where the period is not constant.

This study focuses on identifying the nearest negative imaginary system for a given proper rational system, assuming the target system is negative imaginary. We develop an algorithm grounded in the LMI characterization of negative imaginary systems, allowing for the identification of nearest negative imaginary systems that are either strictly stable or asymptotically stable. Our results demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of the asymptotic solution under certain conditions. Moreover, we establish that the identified system is near-optimal in minimizing the H∞ norm of the error transfer function between the original and target systems. Our findings are further validated through the examination of a practical case study involving a flexible structure actuated by hydraulic actuators.

The goal of this research is to develop a method for continuously learning in end-to-end automatic speech recognition systems using a single language. We investigate the effects of different learning strategies, including the use of rehearsal and feature-based approaches, on the performance of speech recognition models. Our findings indicate that incorporating rehearsal can significantly improve speech recognition accuracy, especially when the model is trained on a small dataset. We also found that certain techniques, such as the use of a specific loss function, can help mitigate the issue of catastrophic forgetting. Ultimately, our experiments demonstrate that a combination of these methods can achieve state-of-the-art results on a benchmark dataset, while also maintaining good performance on a previous dataset.

This study presents a sentiment analysis system that incorporates multilingual word embeddings and a deep learning-based classifier to address the SemEval-2020 Task 9: Sentiment Analysis in Mixed-Language Environments. The system was evaluated on a dataset of Malay-English mixed-language texts, yielding a high degree of accuracy and outperforming other systems in the competition. The analysis also revealed that the system's performance was significantly influenced by the quality of the word embeddings used.

We suggest a novel framework for the radiative seesaw model, incorporating an extended particle sector with a specific gauge group, to address the neutrino mass and cosmological baryon asymmetry issues. This model's gauge symmetry is broken at a low energy scale, resulting in the generation of a Majorana mass for right-handed neutrinos. We examine the cosmological implications of the model, particularly the thermal freeze-out of the lightest right-handed neutrino, which serves as dark matter, and the out-of-equilibrium decay of the next heaviest neutrino, which produces the observed baryon asymmetry. We find that the model's parameters are consistent with neutrino oscillation data and cosmological observations, and that the model's predictions for the dark matter relic density and baryon asymmetry are in agreement with the observed values.

In the field of recommender systems, predicting user preferences is a critical task.
Deep learning models, such as neural networks, have been successfully applied to this problem.
A novel approach, called the Product-based Neural Network (PBNN), is presented in this research.
The PBNN model is designed to accurately forecast user preferences by utilizing a product-based architecture.
The model's effectiveness is demonstrated through its ability to outperform existing state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmark datasets.

This research focuses on cell-free networks enhanced by intelligent reflecting surfaces, with the goal of minimizing the sum rate under uncertain channel conditions. To address this, a robust joint design of beamforming and IRS phase shifting is proposed, with the former being restricted to a specific set of beamforming vectors. The resulting optimization problem is complex and non-convex due to the presence of probabilistic constraints. To resolve this, a two-stage algorithm is developed, with the first stage employing a semidefinite relaxation technique to obtain a feasible solution, and the second stage utilizing a sequential majorization-minimization approach to refine the results. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

The branch predictor is a crucial component in modern high-performance processors, and its efficiency is vital for optimizing performance. However, dynamic branch prediction techniques are limited by their inability to adapt to complex branch patterns, which can lead to performance degradation. To address this challenge, machine learning-based approaches have been developed, but a comprehensive review of these methods is necessary to identify their strengths and limitations. This survey paper provides an in-depth analysis of deep learning-based branch predictors, including their underlying principles, key features, and performance outcomes. Furthermore, it highlights the current state of the field and identifies areas for future research.

This research introduces an innovative approach to active camera control, leveraging imitation learning to develop an optimal camera control strategy. By utilizing a convolutional neural network, our method trains the system to identify the most effective camera angle for a given scene, based on a dataset of images with varying angles. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to traditional approaches, as evidenced by its ability to capture a target with high accuracy and minimal loss, while also showcasing its ability to generalize well in real-world scenarios.

We examine a specific Gibbs measure on the second-order SOS model with the 1D lattice, characterized by the measure's invariance under the action of the dihedral group, and we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for its existence. This existence is equivalent to the presence of a particular Gibbs measure on the star-triangle model with the 1D lattice, and we further show that the corresponding measure on the SOS model satisfies a particular non-linear difference equation of the second order.

A novel approach to calculating the resonant energy transfer rate between two photons within any medium has been developed. This approach involves utilizing the Fokker-Planck equation to model the medium's influence on photons, and then applying a mathematical transformation to derive the energy transfer rate. This rate is expressed as a function of the medium's properties and the photons' characteristics, and it can be used to predict the behavior of entangled photons in various environments.

The discovery of neutrino oscillations has revolutionized the field of neutrino physics, fundamentally altering our understanding of neutrino behavior. This has led to a surge in interest in neutrino oscillation research, with a primary focus on determining the neutrino mass hierarchy and CP-violating phase. This article delves into the current status of neutrino mass hierarchy and CP-violation studies, as well as explores the future of neutrino physics, highlighting the potential of next-generation neutrino experiments to make groundbreaking discoveries.

A widely used method for estimating causal effects is linear regression, 
which is often applied to analyze the impact of a treatment on an outcome.
However, the potential for confounding variables to bias the results makes it 
essential to consider the influence of covariates in the model.
In this study, we examine the implications of using linear regression for 
causal inference, focusing on the role of covariates and their weights.
We demonstrate that the weights used in linear regression are not fixed but 
rather depend on the characteristics of the data, including the distribution of 
treatment and covariates.
Furthermore, we show that the weights used in linear regression can lead to 
biased estimates of causal effects when there is a relationship between the 
covariates and the outcome.
To address this issue, we propose a new method for adjusting the weights used 
in linear regression, which takes into account the relationship between the 
covariates and the outcome.
We provide a theoretical analysis of the proposed method and demonstrate its 
effectiveness through simulations and real-world data analysis.
Our results suggest that the proposed method can improve the accuracy of 
estimates of causal effects, especially in situations where the covariates are 
strongly related to the outcome.
In conclusion, our study highlights the importance of considering the 
implied weights of linear regression when using it for causal inference.

The damping of inter-area oscillations in power systems is a crucial aspect of maintaining stability, and it can be effectively addressed using the damping control capabilities of voltage source converters (VSCs). This study introduces a model-free control approach for VSCs, which utilizes a decentralized control structure and does not rely on the power system model. The proposed method is based on a distributed observer, which enables the VSCs to estimate the dynamic modes of the power system without the need for centralized communication. The decentralized control structure allows for efficient implementation and communication, and it does not require power flow data. The proposed method is validated through simulations on a 10-machine power system, and it is also applied to a larger 118-bus power system to demonstrate its effectiveness. The results show that the proposed method can significantly improve the damping of inter-area oscillations and enhance the power system's stability.

We investigate the concept of subradiance in the steady state of a two-atom system, which is being continuously exposed to weak light. Our research reveals that subradiance in the system's steady state can be controlled through the introduction of a decay process. Furthermore, we found that the presence of decay can lead to the emergence of a completely dark steady state, which exhibits characteristics of subradiance.

We examine the nonlinear scalar field equation $\partial_t^2\phi - \partial_x^2\phi + V'(\phi) = 0$ in the context of a potential $V(\phi) = \frac{1}{2}(\phi^2 - 1)^2 + \epsilon\phi^3$ with $\epsilon > 0$. Our study focuses on the kink solution $\phi_K(x) = \tanh(x)$, which is a stationary solution to the equation. We consider the linearized dynamics around this kink solution and find that it has a discrete spectrum with a single simple eigenvalue $\lambda_0$ and two Jordan blocks associated with $\lambda_0$. We then derive a modified version of the virial theorem and use it to establish a kink-internal mode resonance. Finally, we apply the method of energy scattering to demonstrate that the kink is asymptotically stable under odd perturbations.

The Japan Proton Accelerator Research Complex (J-PARC) serves as a high-intensity facility for conducting high-precision experiments in the GeV energy range. This article outlines the current status of J-PARC's hadron physics experiments, with a particular emphasis on the facility's capabilities in studying color transparency. Notably, J-PARC is the sole facility in the world that can produce pion-proton elastic scattering at GeV energies with high precision. Moreover, it is the only facility in Japan capable of conducting a comprehensive study of the exclusive reaction, where a pion is produced in association with a proton and a neutron.

Recent studies have demonstrated that training models with virtual adversarial examples can significantly enhance their robustness. However, the current methods are limited by the requirement of an oracle that can generate optimal perturbations. To address this, we introduce a new technique called Virtual Adversarial Consistency Training (VACT), which enables the model to learn from a discrete, virtual adversarial example. By incorporating this virtual example into the consistency training process, VACT achieves better robustness and accuracy compared to previous approaches. Experimental results on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets confirm the effectiveness of VACT.

In endoscopic video polyp detection, leveraging multiple frames can significantly enhance detection accuracy. However, the conventional approach of processing each frame independently often results in redundant computations and suboptimal performance. To address this, we introduce a novel framework that combines spatial and temporal features from multiple frames to improve polyp detection accuracy. Our approach involves a multi-frame collaboration module that extracts and fuses spatial and temporal features from multiple frames, followed by a refinement process to enhance the quality of the learned features. We also propose a novel attention-based module that enables the model to selectively focus on salient features from multiple frames. Our experiments on the Kvasir dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, achieving a substantial improvement in detection accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches.

The study of $^{57}$Zn's $\beta$-delayed proton emission has been conducted using the $\gamma$-ray tracking array GRETINA, which has successfully identified the $^{56}$Ni nucleus as a stable intermediate state. This discovery confirms that $^{56}$Ni serves as a crucial stepping stone in the $^{57}$Zn proton emission process. The research has also provided essential data on the $^{56}$Ni nucleus's mass and excited state properties, which are vital for understanding the nuclear reactions that occur in the universe. The findings have significant implications for the study of supernovae and the creation of elements in the universe.

We have expanded the Manin-Mumford theorem to include a broader category of varieties, specifically those that are part of a family of curves with a particular type of structure. This family is characterized by its ability to be mapped onto a curve, with the resulting map having a degree of two or more. Our research demonstrates that any set of points within these families, with a particular type of relationship to their structure, must be contained within a specific, lower-dimensional subset of the family. This lower-dimensional subset is defined by specific sub-structures within the family, with a dimension that is one less than the number of points being considered.

The detection of gamma-ray emission from pulsars is a significant discovery in high-energy astrophysics. Pulsars, which emit gamma rays at high energies, are crucial for understanding the gamma-ray sky. Researchers have been studying pulsars using ground-based Cherenkov telescopes, which have led to the identification of several gamma-ray emitting pulsars. In this study, we report the results of a long-term observation of a specific pulsar, PSR J1023+0038, using the VERITAS telescope. Our findings show that this pulsar does not emit gamma rays at high energies, with a 95% confidence level. We also present the results of gamma-ray emission searches in the vicinity of other pulsars, including PSR J1023+0038, with the VERITAS telescope.

This paper investigates the long-term behavior of solutions to reaction-diffusion equations with nonlocal boundary conditions on domains with irregular boundaries. We establish the existence of global attractors and exponential stability for these attractors, and demonstrate that the semigroup generated by the equations exhibits a pullback attractor in an infinite-dimensional environment.

The identification of Ultra-Compact Dwarf galaxies is crucial for understanding the formation of globular clusters and the evolution of galaxies. However, distinguishing UCDs from globular clusters in large galaxy surveys is a complex task due to their similarities in size and brightness. This research aims to develop an AI-based approach to identify UCDs in galaxy images, utilizing the XGBoost algorithm and a deep learning model. By analyzing the images of galaxy clusters, the AI models can automatically detect and classify UCDs. To validate the AI models, the researchers used the Hubble Space Telescope images of the Virgo cluster and the Fornax cluster, and the results showed that the AI models successfully identified UCDs in the images. Furthermore, the researchers used the LIME and SHAP explainability techniques to understand how the AI models make predictions, and the results revealed that the AI models can accurately identify UCDs in the images.

The recommender systems community has been employing simulations to evaluate and compare algorithms, but their application in the industry remains largely unexplored. This paper delves into the use of simulations within an industry setting, specifically focusing on an in-vivo experiment conducted by Netflix. It also examines the advantages and disadvantages of using simulations within the industry, and offers insights into how these pros and cons were navigated during the Netflix experiment. Additionally, the paper discusses potential future directions for utilizing simulations within the industry.

This study examines the extreme tail behavior of heavy-tailed distributions, specifically focusing on those with a heavy tail. The research investigates the applicability of a commonly used statistical test for heavy-tailed distributions, which is typically used to test the mean of a sample. The study derives the limiting distribution of a sample mean, after being truncated at a certain point, and explores the asymptotic properties of the test. The results indicate that the test can be effective in detecting differences in the mean of samples from heavy-tailed distributions, but it may not be effective in detecting differences in samples from other types of distributions. The research also provides an example of how the test can be used in practice, specifically in the context of a study on the effectiveness of a new drug treatment.

A novel Sinc-based convolutional neural network is proposed for motor imagery EEG signal classification, which incorporates a Sinc filter bank to extract relevant features from the input data. This network is capable of learning complex, non-linear relationships between EEG signals and motor imagery tasks, and can be trained using a variety of loss functions. Our approach is evaluated on a publicly available dataset of motor imagery EEG signals, and the results demonstrate that the Sinc-based network outperforms traditional convolutional neural networks in terms of accuracy and robustness.

The issue of incompatible kidney transplants is a significant problem in the medical field.  A patient's blood type and their spouse's are incompatible, making a kidney donation from the spouse impossible without a medical intervention.  A blood compatibility test is a simple and non-invasive procedure that can determine if the spouse's kidney is compatible with the patient's body.  Incompatible transplants can be made possible with a medical treatment known as desensitization, but this treatment comes with significant risks and complications.  We have developed a model that incorporates a patient's medical history and the potential for complications to determine the optimal time for a patient to accept an incompatible kidney transplant.  The model also accounts for the possibility of patients being referred to a desensitization center and the potential for complications to occur.  The model's predictions are based on real-world data and have been validated by comparing them to actual outcomes.  The model's predictions show that patients who wait for a compatible kidney transplant are more likely to experience a kidney failure than if they accept an incompatible kidney transplant.  The model's predictions also show that patients who accept an incompatible kidney transplant are more likely to experience a kidney failure than patients who wait for a compatible kidney transplant.  The model's predictions can be used to inform patients about the potential risks and benefits of accepting an incompatible kidney transplant.

This paper presents a novel hybrid approach that combines Hidden Markov Models (HMM) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance their individual performance capabilities. The proposed model leverages the strengths of both HMM and LSTM, resulting in improved performance. Experimental evaluations were conducted on the MSRA dataset for Chinese word segmentation and on the standard English and Chinese datasets for part-of-speech tagging. The results demonstrate that the hybrid model outperforms standalone HMM and LSTM-LSTM networks in both tasks.

This research paper explores the boundedness and compactness of generalized Volterra integral operators and specific Toeplitz operators within weighted Bergman spaces, with particular focus on how the properties of weight functions influence these operators.

We have developed an efficient method for compressing neural models that excel in multi-task and cross-lingual settings. This method leverages shared parameters across different tasks and language models to achieve significant compression. We tested our approach on various compressed models, including those with 100M, 300M, and 700M parameters, and found that they can be compressed to a 1/6th of their size with minimal impact on performance. Notably, our 1/6th-sized model outperforms the state-of-the-art models developed by Google and Microsoft, which are 2/3rd its size.

We suggest an approach to calculate low rank approximations of positive semi-definite symmetric matrices by combining Gaussian elimination with volume sampling techniques. This method is compared to two other approaches, one utilizing singular value decomposition and another employing Jacobi rotation. The proposed approach offers the benefit of operating with integer values, thereby eliminating floating point arithmetic.

Wikipedia's extensive use of wiki markup in its articles, a format that's easy to write but hard to read, poses a challenge for researchers who need to analyze the content. To address this issue, we've developed WikiHist.html, a tool that converts the entire English Wikipedia's article revisions into readable HTML format. This allows for easier comprehension of the content, and we've also created a user-friendly interface to search through the content and display the results. To showcase the potential of WikiHist.html, we've used it to study the evolution of Wikipedia's article revisions over time, revealing that articles that have undergone significant changes tend to have more edits and are more likely to be deleted.

We investigate the emergence of topological networks in twisted bilayers, specifically focusing on polar merons and antimerons. These topological defects arise from the interplay of the Coulomb interaction and the Zeeman field, which stabilizes the antiferromagnetic phase in twisted bilayers. The interplay of these factors leads to the formation of domain walls with a polar gradient, which can host topological defects. The resulting network of these defects exhibits a non-trivial topological structure, characterized by the presence of zero-energy modes. The Zeeman field breaks inversion symmetry, leading to the formation of polar merons and antimerons with different topological charges. The resulting network of topological defects exhibits a rich phase diagram, which can be tuned by varying the Zeeman field and the twist angle. The resulting topological structure is characterized by the presence of zero-energy modes, which are robust against disorder and can be used to probe the underlying physics of the system.

Researchers have developed a novel method to manipulate the movement of individual particles within a liquid crystal by utilizing a surface with a wavy pattern. This approach allows for the generation of diverse trajectories, including circular paths, figure-eight patterns, and elliptical paths, by adjusting the surface's wavelength and waveforms. A theoretical model has been established to explain the underlying mechanisms of this phenomenon, and experimental results have been conducted to validate the theoretical predictions. This technique offers a flexible and efficient means of controlling particle motion within a liquid crystal, and may have potential applications in the development of advanced colloidal devices.

The unique shapes of small celestial bodies, such as rubble-pile asteroids, are a result of the balance between their internal cohesion and external gravitational forces. As a result, these objects can exhibit a wide range of shapes, from spherical to elongated, and their surface characteristics can be significantly influenced by their shape. Our research focuses on the surface temperature distribution of spherical and elongated rubble-pile asteroids during a close encounter with a planet, revealing that the shape of these objects has a profound impact on their surface temperature. Our findings indicate that the temperature distribution on the asteroid's surface is highly sensitive to its shape, and that the temperature can vary by up to 100 K during a close encounter. This research has significant implications for our understanding of the surface characteristics of celestial bodies and the potential for detecting changes in their surface temperature during close encounters with planets.

Biological molecules' behavior is significantly influenced by the occurrence of rare events, which are difficult to simulate using classical computers. A new method has been developed to study these rare events by utilizing quantum computers. The method involves breaking down the rare event into a series of smaller, more manageable events, which are then simulated using quantum computers. The approach is demonstrated through its application to the study of protein folding, specifically in the case of the villin head peptide. The results show that the method can accurately model the protein's behavior, including its rare unfolding event, and can be used to study the dynamics of complex biological systems.

The development of Monte-Carlo Applications for Partially Polarised Inverse External-Compton Scattering (MAPPIES) is presented, a tool designed to simulate inverse Compton scattering in astrophysical sources with varying levels of initial polarization. This code can model polarization in the final outcome by taking into account the polarization of incident photons, electron spin polarization, and magnetic field polarization. It also accounts for the polarization of the final photon in non-linear scattering scenarios. To showcase the capabilities of MAPPIES, we have applied it to model the polarization of inverse Compton emission from blazars and gamma-ray bursts, with the results indicating that the polarization of incident photons can have a substantial impact on the polarization of the final outcome.

The Arctic's sea ice thickness distribution is a crucial factor in understanding the Arctic's sea ice system and its response to climate change. This study uses satellite data to examine the Arctic's sea ice thickness distribution from 2002 to 2018, revealing a consistent pattern of thin ice expansion in the summer and thick ice expansion in the winter. This research also found that the Arctic's sea ice thickness distribution has been shifting towards thinner ice over time, a trend linked to the declining extent of multi-year ice. This study's findings are supported by a new method for estimating sea ice thickness distribution that combines satellite data with a statistical model, allowing for a more accurate representation of the Arctic's sea ice thickness distribution.

This study focuses on analyzing the Weierstrass semigroup at specific points on curves of type $\mathcal{X}_{a,b}$ defined over finite fields. These curves are maximal, but not covered by the Hermitian curve. It is found that for certain values of $a$ and $b$, the Weierstrass semigroup at specific points on $\mathcal{X}_{a,b}$ is isomorphic to that of a related maximal curve. This new curve, $\mathcal{Y}_c$, is also defined over finite fields and has a specific structure. It is shown that $\mathcal{Y}_c$ can be embedded in $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{F}_{q^m})$ and has a specific structure. It is found that for certain values of $c$, the Weierstrass semigroup at specific points on $\mathcal{Y}_c$ is isomorphic to that of a related maximal curve. This study also provides a specific example of a curve, $\mathcal{X}_{3,2}$, for which the Weierstrass semigroup at specific points is isomorphic to that of a related maximal curve.

The field of singing voice synthesis has seen significant growth in recent years,
with researchers developing a variety of systems that can produce high-quality
singing voices. This survey provides an in-depth analysis of the latest
developments in deep learning-based singing voice synthesis, focusing on the
evolution of the field from its initial deep learning applications to the
current state-of-the-art systems. The survey covers a wide range of techniques,
including those that utilize deep learning to generate singing voices from
monophonic audio, polyphonic audio, and text, as well as those that can
synthesize singing voices from mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and
pitch-accent sequences. The survey also examines the performance of these
systems and their applications in various fields, including entertainment,
education, and healthcare. The survey aims to provide a comprehensive overview
of the current state of the field and to identify areas for future research.

The field of birdsong research has been hindered by the lack of comprehensive audio datasets that include annotations of birdsong types. To address this issue, we have created the NIPS4Bplus dataset, which consists of 2,410 high-quality audio recordings of 27 birds, featuring 1,050 songs and 1,360 fragments. This dataset is notable for its extensive annotations of birdsong types, including 1,500 annotated songs and 2,000 annotated fragments, as well as its inclusion of temporal annotations for 1,800 songs and 2,300 fragments. Additionally, the dataset includes annotations of the sex of 1,400 individuals and the species of 2,410 individuals. To facilitate the development of new methods for birdsong analysis, the dataset is made available for research purposes.

This paper outlines an approach to calibrate event cameras, which enables the use of established image processing techniques in the realm of event-based vision. The presented method involves a straightforward procedure for determining the intrinsic parameters of an event camera, including the spatial resolution, pixel arrangement, and sensitivity. The required calibration can be achieved through the use of a single image or video, captured with a standard camera. The proposed method is versatile and can be applied to various event camera models, including those with different pixel arrangements and resolutions. The authors provide a comprehensive evaluation of their method, including a comparison with the results obtained using a high-resolution calibration setup. The presented approach offers a straightforward and efficient alternative for calibrating event cameras, thereby facilitating their use in practical applications.

Graph learning has become a crucial component of machine learning, enabling the analysis of complex data sets that are structured in a network format. This approach has been successfully applied in a wide range of applications, including social media analysis, natural language processing, and bioinformatics. This study provides a comprehensive review of the current state of graph learning research, focusing on the underlying techniques and methods. The paper first outlines the fundamental concepts of graph learning, then delves into the various techniques used to represent graphs, including feature extraction and embedding techniques. The study also covers a range of graph learning methods, including unsupervised, semi-supervised, and supervised approaches, as well as graph neural networks. The paper concludes by identifying key areas of future research in graph learning, including the development of more advanced graph models, the integration of graph learning with other machine learning techniques, and the application of graph learning to new domains.

A significant challenge in ophthalmology is performing delicate tasks like retinal detachment repair, which can be complicated by the eye's limited visibility and the surgeon's restricted field of view. To overcome this limitation, we've developed a virtual reality system that provides surgeons with a three-dimensional view of the retina, allowing them to navigate the retina's surface more effectively. This system, which utilizes a specialized camera and advanced image processing, can track the surgeon's movements and display a real-time, three-dimensional representation of the retina. By combining this information with the surgeon's field of view, we've created a tool that can help surgeons navigate the retina's surface more accurately and efficiently. Our system has been tested in a series of experiments with both novice and experienced surgeons, and the results show that it can significantly improve surgical outcomes by reducing the time it takes to complete a task and the number of errors made.
